newsitem.title: MALI: Mali gold mine approves Randgold holding.
newsitem.headline: Mali gold mine approves Randgold holding.

text.p: BAMAKO, June 27 - Mali gold mining company Societe Miniere de Loulo (Somilo) approved a majority shareholding bought by South African Randgold Resources Ltd, Somilo company sources said after a Somilo board meeting which ended Thursday.

Randgold bought a 31 percent stake from the government in early June, raising its shareholding to 51 percent from 20 percent. That left the government with a 10 percent stake in Somilo and another 39 percent in the hands of French-Australian group Mine d'Or SA.
Randgold was given the right to buy the further 31 percent stake in Somilo on completion of payments and a mine feasibility study. Sources said payment details had yet to be finalised.

Randgold said after raising its stake in Somilo that combined mining operations from two pits at Loulo and Yalea could involve milling 120,000 tonnes of ore a year with a possible total annual gold output of around 140,000 ounces.
The study would be completed and presented to Somilo's board in June, but a decision on mining was not expected until July at the earliest.

Loulo mine was discovered in 1983 in Mali's gold-rich Kenieba region. Estimated reserves then put at 44 tonnes are now seen totalling around 120 tonnes after a second reserve was found at Yalea, six km from the main site at Loulo, a government statement said on June 23.
Provisional annual production has been put at 4-5 tonnes a year with a total investment of $80 million, it said.
